objective: Replace frozen-input-only interventions with equally trained input-conditioned Encoders, retain the same official SONIC Decoder, and evaluate on new whole physical pairs without selecting a winner.
physical_acceptance: Reuse temporal_pairs.generate_pair and its fixed full-state endpoint/interior/force/solver-budget checks. All rejections retained. Both signs and every window of each pair stay in the same split.
trainable: Only the selected new Encoder; original Encoder, FSQ and both Decoder parameter arrays remain unchanged.
initialization: Reset the selected original BaseModule MLP with the declared seed; identical learned weights across cue conditions within each modality/seed. Not independent full-controller or PPO initializations.

training.method: Local supervised imitation of recorded normalized actions through original SONIC Encoder/FSQ/frozen Decoder; not an official PPO experiment.
training.loss: Mean squared error to both recorded normalized actions; pair signs always balanced.
training.checkpoint_selection: Final fixed-budget checkpoint only. Validation is reported but never used to select a checkpoint, epoch, seed or learning rate.

closed_loop.targets: unchanged prerecorded true reference, with physically simulated zero-control preview tail

marker_noise_probe.scope: Offline input sensitivity of full-future marker Encoder on test references; actual proprioception/labels unchanged. Not a noisy-sensor controller certification.

evaluations.missing_marker_contract: Prove the existing tip-only ambiguity, and reject missing full-marker information rather than treating an unmarked zero as an observed value. No inverse-state claim from ambiguous data.

claim_limits: Equal training budget is not proof that every condition is globally optimally trained.
New Encoder seeds share one fixed previously trained controller/Decoder.
Recorded first-action prediction is not a universal control-performance bound.
Subsecond paired maneuvers are not sustained stability, original SONIC humanoid performance or sim-to-real readiness.
This experiment changes no browser policy, shared service, hardware authority or robot embodiment.
Failure to learn is an experiment/representation gap unless a required physical structure is demonstrably absent.
